title: Failure of the pivotal probability formula
statement: On the one-dimensional sign cube, let $f(x)=x$, take bias parameter $p=1/4$, output sign $-1$, and coordinate $1$. Under the product distribution with probabilities $3/4$ for $+1$ and $1/4$ for $-1$, the probability that $f(x)=-1$ and flipping the coordinate changes the output is not equal to the mass of $-1$ times the squared $L^2$ distance of $f$ from its projection onto functions independent of that coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: The function is the coordinate dictator $f(x)=x$
The specified coordinate is the sole coordinate
